subject: maths
title: Multiply and Divide by 10, 100 and 1,000
seo_title: Year 5 Multiply and Divide by 10, 100 and 1,000 Worksheets: Whole Numbers and Decimals
standard_text: Multiply and divide whole numbers and those involving decimals by 10, 100 and 1,000.
meta_desc: Free Year 5 maths worksheets on multiplying and dividing by 10, 100 and 1,000 for the National Curriculum: whole numbers and decimals, place value charts, missing numbers, unit conversions and money problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: The digits move, the decimal point stays still: left to multiply, right to divide.
key_sub: 1 place for 10, 2 places for 100, 3 places for 1,000. 45 × 100 = 4,500, 450 ÷ 100 = 4.5, 0.36 × 100 = 36, 3.2 ÷ 100 = 0.032. Adding a zero to 3.2 gives 3.20, which is still 3.2.
body_html:
The digits move, the point stays still

When you multiply by 10, 100 or 1,000, every digit moves to the left. When you divide, every digit moves to the right.

CalculationEvery digit moves
× 10 or ÷ 101 place
× 100 or ÷ 1002 places
× 1,000 or ÷ 1,0003 places

The decimal point does not move. Write 0 in any empty place up to the ones.

Dividing can give a decimal

Example

7,000 ÷ 1,000

Every digit moves 3 places to the right. The 7 goes from the thousands to the ones.

Answer: 7

Decimals work the same way

Missing numbers: use the inverse

× and ÷ undo each other. To find ? in ? × 100 = 470, work out 470 ÷ 100 = 4.7. Then check: 4.7 × 100 = 470.

Example

A pen costs £1.25. How much do 100 pens cost?

1.25 × 100: every digit moves 2 places to the left. 1.25 × 100 = 125.

Answer: £125

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
3.2 × 10 = 3.20 (just adding a zero)3.20 is the same as 3.2. Move the digits 1 place: 32
450 ÷ 100 = 45 or 0.45÷ 100 moves the digits exactly 2 places: 4.5
0.36 × 100 = 0.3600The digits move 2 places to the left: 36
306 × 100 = 36,000Keep the 0 that holds a place: 30,600
Moving the digits the wrong way× makes the number bigger (left); ÷ makes it smaller (right)

faq.q: How do you multiply by 10, 100 and 1,000 in Year 5?
faq.a: Move every digit 1, 2 or 3 places to the left and keep the decimal point still. Write 0 in empty places up to the ones, so 45 × 100 = 4,500 and 0.36 × 100 = 36.

faq.q: How do you divide a decimal by 100?
faq.a: Move every digit 2 places to the right and write 0 in the empty places up to the ones. For example, 3.2 ÷ 100 = 0.032.

faq.q: Why is “just add a zero” wrong?
faq.a: It only works for whole numbers. With decimals it gives the wrong answer: 3.2 × 10 is 32, not 3.20, because 3.20 has the same value as 3.2.

faq.q: Where is multiplying by 10, 100 and 1,000 used in real life?
faq.a: Converting units (3.5 kg = 3,500 g, 250 cm = 2.5 m) and working out prices for 10, 100 or 1,000 items. It is part of the Year 5 National Curriculum for multiplication and division.

9 × 1,000: every digit moves 3 places to the left. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places up to the ones. 9 × 1,000 = 9,000.

items.q: Which calculation does the chart show?
items.e: Every digit moved 2 places to the left, so it is × 100. 36 × 100 = 3,600.
306 × 100: every digit moves 2 places to the left. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places up to the ones. 306 × 100 = 30,600. (Keep the 0 in the tens of 306: it holds a place.)
6,300 is 63 with two zeros in the empty places: the digits moved 2 places to the left. So it is × 100.

470 × 1,000: every digit moves 3 places to the left. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places up to the ones. 470 × 1,000 = 470,000. (The 0 in 470 is not one of the 3 places.)
2,500 × 10: every digit moves 1 place to the left. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places up to the ones. 2,500 × 10 = 25,000.
Use the inverse: 5,200 ÷ 10. Every digit moves 1 place to the right: 520. Check: 520 × 10 = 5,200.

Use the inverse: 39,000 ÷ 1,000. Every digit moves 3 places to the right: 39. Check: 39 × 1,000 = 39,000.
715 became 71,500: the 7 moved from the hundreds to the ten thousands. That is 2 places to the left, so it is × 100.

items.q: The chart shows 284 × 100 = 28,400. What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: 284 × 100 = 28,400. Every digit moved 2 places to the left, so the 2 is now in the ten thousands place. Its value is 2 ten thousands.

items.q: Which number is 100 times bigger than 3,070?
items.e: 100 times bigger means × 100. Every digit moves 2 places to the left: 3,070 × 100 = 307,000. (3,170 adds 100.)

items.q: The chart shows 41.6 ÷ 100 = 0.416. What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: 41.6 ÷ 100 = 0.416. Every digit moved 2 places to the right, so the 6 is now in the thousandths place. Its value is 6 thousandths.

items.q: Which is the same as 0.4 ÷ 10?
Which calculation does not equal 48?
A bag of potatoes has a mass of 3.5 kg. What is its mass in grams?
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g, so multiply by 1,000. The digits move 3 places to the left: 3.5 × 1,000 = 3,500 g.

items.q: A school buys 100 notebooks at £2.45 each. How much do they cost altogether?
items.e: £2.45 × 100: the digits move 2 places to the left. 2.45 × 100 = 245, so they cost £245.00. (£102.45 adds 100.)

items.q: A garden path has 100 paving slabs in a row. Each slab is 0.45 m long. How long is the path?
items.e: 0.45 × 100: the digits move 2 places to the left. The path is 45 m long.

items.q: A plant is 250 cm tall. How tall is it in metres?
items.e: 100 cm = 1 m, so divide by 100. The digits move 2 places to the right: 250 ÷ 100 = 2.5 m.

items.q: A watering can holds 4.2 litres of water. How many millilitres is that?
Arjun uses 750 g of flour to make bread. How many kilograms is that?
items.e: 1,000 g = 1 kg, so divide by 1,000. The digits move 3 places to the right: 750 ÷ 1,000 = 0.75 kg.

items.q: A pack of 10 bags of crisps costs £6.50. How much is one bag?
items.e: £6.50 ÷ 10: the digits move 1 place to the right. £0.65 = 65p. Check: 65p × 10 = 650p = £6.50.

items.q: A box of 100 stickers costs £3. How much is one sticker?
items.e: £3 ÷ 100: the digits move 2 places to the right. £0.03 = 3p. (30p is £3 ÷ 10.)

items.q: Freya runs 0.8 km every day for 10 days. How far does she run altogether?
items.e: 0.8 × 10: the 8 moves from the tenths to the ones. Freya runs 8 km. (0.80 km just adds a zero.)

items.q: A lorry carries 1,000 boxes. Each box has a mass of 2.4 kg. What is the total mass?
items.e: 2.4 × 1,000: the digits move 3 places to the left. The total mass is 2,400 kg.

items.q: A 3.6 m length of ribbon is cut into 10 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
items.e: 3.6 ÷ 10: the digits move 1 place to the right. Each piece is 0.36 m (36 cm).

items.q: A PE teacher buys 10 footballs at £8.99 each. How much does she pay?
items.e: £8.99 × 10: the digits move 1 place to the left. 8.99 × 10 = 89.9, so she pays £89.90. (£80.99 multiplies only the pounds.)

items.q: A 5,600 m cycle route goes round the park. How many kilometres is that?
Fabric for the school play costs £4.75 per metre. How much do 100 m cost?
items.e: £4.75 × 100: the digits move 2 places to the left. 100 m cost £475.00.

items.q: A real car is 100 times as long as a model car. The model is 4.3 cm long. How long is the real car?
items.e: The real car is 100 times as long: 4.3 × 100 = 430 cm, which is 4.3 m.

items.q: A class pays £245 for 100 museum tickets. How much is one ticket?
items.e: £245 ÷ 100: the digits move 2 places to the right. One ticket costs £2.45. (£24.50 is £245 ÷ 10.)

items.q: A shop has 1,000 bottles of water. Each holds 1.5 litres. How much water is that altogether?
items.e: 1.5 × 1,000: the digits move 3 places to the left: 1,500 litres.

items.q: Kai buys 10 pencils at 35p each. He pays with a £5 note. How much change does he get?
A cook uses 0.35 kg of rice for 10 school dinners. How much rice is needed for 1,000 school dinners?
items.e: 1,000 dinners is 100 lots of 10 dinners. So multiply by 100: 0.35 × 100 = 35 kg. (350 kg multiplies by 1,000, but 0.35 kg is for 10 dinners, not 1.)

items.q: A pile of 1,000 sheets of paper is 95 mm tall. How thick is one sheet?
items.e: 95 ÷ 1,000: the digits move 3 places to the right. Write 0 in the ones and tenths: one sheet is 0.095 mm thick.
